title: AVM Founder Systems Archive (Visual System)

preExistingSystemAssessment.conclusion: AVM's existing design system already satisfied nearly all Founder Systems Archive requirements before this pass
evidence: dark-first with prefers-color-scheme + explicit [data-theme] toggle, both themes already contrast-audited (docs/mark-2-release-audit.md)
serif --font-display headings (editorial identity, distinct from TMI's grotesk/mono system-index face)
38rem reading measure + three-tier text color system already tuned for long-form reading
single restrained --color-accent used only for focus/buttons/eyebrow, status communicated via text+role=status never color alone
3px/6px border radii already crisp and disciplined pre-Mark-13
zero hardcoded colors outside tokens.css across the entire src tree
preExistingSystemAssessment.decision: narrow, additive-only pass (token layer) rather than a redesign, to avoid risking 74 passing e2e checks and to avoid moving AVM's look toward TMI's

changed.description: added a --ff-* semantic alias block inside the existing :root declaration; every alias is a var() reference to an existing AVM token, so light-theme and [data-theme] toggle overrides apply automatically with no duplication

notChanged: the frozen fallback branch (claude/alexander-mathai-placeholder, PR #1) -- never opened

deliberateDeviationFromSharedVocabulary.actualValue: var(--color-accent) -- AVM's own existing orange accent
deliberateDeviationFromSharedVocabulary.reason: the brief's own non-negotiable rule is that AVM must never be visually/semantically collapsed into a TMI corporate identity; giving both properties the literal same accent hue works against that rule. The shared vocabulary is the ROLE of the token (one restrained, scarce accent), not a literal shared hex. --ff-focus-ring follows the same reasoning.

--ff-accent-signal-muted.note: theme-adaptive tint, no hardcoded rgba tuple needed

routesStyledNote: no route or component markup changed; the alias layer applies automatically wherever --color-* is already consumed
